newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes lower vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes lower vs dollar.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee closed slightly lower against the dollar as high call money rates kept many banks sidelined, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.32 to the U.S. currency after opening at 58.29. It closed at 58.27 on Wednesday.
Overnight call money was volatile, rising to 21 percent at one point, dropping down to 16 percent and finally closing at around 18 percent, dealers said.
"Dealers were worried about their positions. People were selling dollars to generate money," a Standard Chartered Bank dealer said.

The Central Bank too has been lethargic towards the greenback, keeping the range unchanged despite overseas movements. On Thursday, it maintained buying and selling levels at 58.2541 and 59.4309, for the third successive day.
Dealers said they expected the Central Bank to keep the range unchanged on Friday as well.
"There was selling pressure but at the same time there was import covering, which prompted the dollar to pick up slightly," a Commercial Bank dealer said.
Dealers said call money has been volatile so far this week as money has been tight, mainly due to quarterly tax payments.
